paper_title: Intrinsically Stretchable Polymer Semiconductors with Good Ductility and High Charge Mobility through Reducing the Central Symmetry of the Conjugated Backbone Units

qa_pairs.question: What is the specific molecular design strategy used to enhance the ductility of diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP)-based conjugated polymers in this study?
qa_pairs.answer: The strategy involves the incorporation of non-centrosymmetric spiro[cycloalkane-1,9'-fluorene] (spiro-fluorene) units into the backbone of the DPP-based polymers. This modification reduces the central symmetry of the polymer chain, which promotes better ductility.
qa_pairs.source_title: Intrinsically Stretchable Polymer Semiconductors with Good Ductility and High Charge Mobility through Reducing the Central Symmetry of the Conjugated Backbone Units

qa_pairs.question: How does the charge mobility of the terpolymer P2 respond to high tensile strain, and what is the maximum reported value?
qa_pairs.answer: The terpolymer P2, which features a cyclopropane-linked spiro-fluorene unit, maintains excellent performance under high strain, achieving a record charge mobility of 3.7 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ even at 150% tensile strain.
qa_pairs.source_title: Intrinsically Stretchable Polymer Semiconductors with Good Ductility and High Charge Mobility through Reducing the Central Symmetry of the Conjugated Backbone Units

qa_pairs.question: Compare the tensile modulus of the parent polymer P1 with the terpolymer P2. What does this change signify?
qa_pairs.answer: The tensile modulus of the parent polymer P1 is 441.1 MPa, while the terpolymer P2 exhibits a significantly lower modulus of 83.7 MPa. This reduction indicates that the incorporation of spiro-fluorene units successfully lowers the mechanical stiffness, making the material more intrinsically stretchable and ductile.
qa_pairs.source_title: Intrinsically Stretchable Polymer Semiconductors with Good Ductility and High Charge Mobility through Reducing the Central Symmetry of the Conjugated Backbone Units

qa_pairs.question: How does reducing the backbone symmetry of the polymer affect its crystalline structure and subsequent mechanical and electrical properties?
qa_pairs.answer: Reducing the symmetry of the conjugated backbone prevents the formation of large, ordered crystalline domains, which leads to decreased thin-film crystallinity and lower mechanical stiffness (improved ductility). However, charge transport is maintained because the polymer chains still form small, densely packed crystalline domains that facilitate efficient carrier movement.
qa_pairs.source_title: Intrinsically Stretchable Polymer Semiconductors with Good Ductility and High Charge Mobility through Reducing the Central Symmetry of the Conjugated Backbone Units

qa_pairs.question: Why do the terpolymers P2-P5 exhibit shorter π-π stacking distances than the parent polymer P1?
qa_pairs.answer: The terpolymers P2-P5 have π-π stacking distances of approximately 3.76 Å to 3.78 Å, which are shorter than P1's 3.85 Å. This is because the spiro-fluorene units lack the bulky branching alkyl chains found in other units, reducing steric hindrance and allowing the polymer chains to pack more densely.
qa_pairs.source_title: Intrinsically Stretchable Polymer Semiconductors with Good Ductility and High Charge Mobility through Reducing the Central Symmetry of the Conjugated Backbone Units

qa_pairs.question: What is the operational stability of the P2 terpolymer when subjected to repeated mechanical deformation?
qa_pairs.answer: P2 demonstrates high operational stability under cyclic stress, retaining a charge mobility of 1.4 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ after 1000 stretching-releasing cycles at 50% strain.
qa_pairs.source_title: Intrinsically Stretchable Polymer Semiconductors with Good Ductility and High Charge Mobility through Reducing the Central Symmetry of the Conjugated Backbone Units

qa_pairs.question: Describe the methodology used to measure the tensile moduli of the polymer thin films.
qa_pairs.answer: The tensile moduli were determined using mechanical buckling metrology. This involves measuring the periodicity of wrinkles that form when the polymer films are transferred onto a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) substrate.
qa_pairs.source_title: Intrinsically Stretchable Polymer Semiconductors with Good Ductility and High Charge Mobility through Reducing the Central Symmetry of the Conjugated Backbone Units

qa_pairs.question: Based on DFT calculations, how does the incorporation of spiro-fluorene units change the physical conformation of the DPP-thiophene backbone?
qa_pairs.answer: DFT calculations indicate that the spiro-fluorene units disrupt the planarity of the backbone, resulting in a non-planar and bending conformation. The connection bonds (formerly C-Br bonds transformed into C-C bonds) form a non-colinear angle ranging from approximately 156.5° to 158.6°.
qa_pairs.source_title: Intrinsically Stretchable Polymer Semiconductors with Good Ductility and High Charge Mobility through Reducing the Central Symmetry of the Conjugated Backbone Units
